correctness.rationale: Reassessed the quorum-comparison repair. For each fixed z, x+ρy=ρ(1−z)+(1−ρ)x; among 0<z<1 the unique optimum in x is at x=0, and the remaining beta-shaped factor peaks only at z=h/n. The weighted benefit and advantage are constant at ω=0; the new text explicitly limits weighted uniqueness to ω>0 and distinguishes normalized ceilings when ω=0. The sign of the adjacent binomial-peak ratio is controlled by the strict increase of (1+1/u)^u. For s≥2 the risk-factor ratio is 1−1/(Σ_{i=0}^{s−1}ρ^(−i)), strictly falling from 1 to (s−1)/s. In the late-quorum case the binomial ratio is strictly between 1 and s/(s−1), by the two strict log bounds log(1+t)<t and log(1+t)>t/(1+t). These yield the exact unique crossing including equality, while symmetry of the binomial peak and the strictly falling risk factor give the unique first quorum, also when n=2. For N=5 the ratio is (9/8)/(1+ρ) and 765/2048<3/8<405/1024 as stated. Also checked the withdrawn dynamics: monotone z/x confines the trajectory to a compact set missing the unique normalized maximizer and yields its uniform-in-time gap; at z=0 the scalar edge bracket is increasing and the transverse rate at an interior edge equilibrium is −k. The vanishing perturbation and isolated scalar zeros justify convergence but do not make it novel. The frozen exact-rational checker was read, not run; the reported 13,680 composition cases and finitely sampled comparisons do not prove the general crossover or the original dynamics. The repaired proof independently establishes the comparisons.

value.rationale: The comparative statics distinguish a globally optimal smallest quorum from nonmonotone behavior among larger quorums. The crossing theorem identifies exactly where the effect of an adjacent quorum increment reverses, at arbitrary group size; it yields strict incentive differences at intermediate costs without conflating them with stable coexistence. This is a useful structural property of the modeled risk-weighted incentive ceiling beyond its already known formula.
